notes: Panel tools: what an agent may ask the AI Studio panel (the browser) to do. MCP tool format: name, description, inputSchema.
The panel keeps the same list (aistudio-app: Benchmarking/src/features/coremind/tools/panel-tools.json) and runs each tool; its tests check every one here has a client tool.
None of them writes or deletes: they navigate, filter, open logs and prefill forms or confirmations, and the user clicks. Real writes go through the backend's MCP tools, with approval.

Kept browser-only, never offered to an agent: fill_input and click_element (with a click they could start or delete), set_style (could hide or fake parts of the page), list_fields (only serves those).

tools.name: panel/navigate
tools.description: Go to a section of the app.
tools.x-backend: Every page shows data from aistudio-server (/api/v1/*).

tools.name: panel/go_back
tools.description: Go back to the previous page.

tools.name: panel/filter_benchmarks
tools.description: Filter the Benchmarks table and chart. Pass only the filters to set; omitted ones are cleared.
tools.x-backend: GET /api/v1/benchmarks accepts model, gpu_type, node_ip, precision, concurrency, input_tokens, output_tokens. After the agent finds runs (list_benchmarks), it can show the same rows on the page.

tools.name: panel/reset_filters
tools.description: Clear all benchmark table filters.
tools.x-backend: Clears the GET /api/v1/benchmarks filters.

tools.name: panel/set_benchmark_type
tools.description: Switch the benchmark chart metric.
tools.x-backend: Chooses which metric the chart plots (throughput / TTFT / TPOT).

tools.name: panel/show_benchmarks_as
tools.description: Switch the Benchmarks results between the chart and the table.
tools.x-backend: Same data (GET /api/v1/benchmarks); lets the agent point at exact rows.
tools.x-frontend: Set the Chart/Table toggle on the Benchmarks page.

tools.name: panel/show_run
tools.description: Show one benchmark run on the Benchmarks page: filter the table to it and open the table view.
tools.x-backend: GET /api/v1/benchmarks?run_id= and GET /api/v1/benchmarks/{run_id}. The agent names runs by id in its answers (compare, diagnose).
tools.x-frontend: Navigate to Benchmarks, filter by run_id (add run_id to the filters store), switch to table.

tools.name: panel/view_run_progress
tools.description: Open the progress drawer for a running or finished benchmark and stream its logs.

task_id.description: Task id of the run, e.g. wl-20261105-1a2b3c.

model.description: Model name, for the drawer title.

node_ip.description: Node IP, for the drawer title.

tools.x-backend: GET /api/v1/benchmarks/{task_id}/logs/stream (SSE) and /status. Follows start_workload, or "why did my run fail?".

tools.name: panel/start_benchmark
tools.description: Open the Start Benchmark wizard.
tools.x-backend: Opens the wizard that ends in POST /api/v1/benchmarks/start.

tools.name: panel/prefill_benchmark
tools.description: Open the Start Benchmark wizard with the node, model and optional settings already filled in, and go to the review step. It never starts the run: the user clicks Start.
tools.x-backend: POST /api/v1/benchmarks/start needs model_name + node_ips + config; GET /api/v1/models/config gives the defaults. One call instead of several set_benchmark_field calls (fewer tokens).
tools.x-frontend: openStartBenchmarkWizard(), then the wizard bridge: setField for each value, next() to the review step.

tools.name: panel/set_benchmark_field
tools.description: Fill one field of the Start Benchmark wizard, opening the wizard if needed. Use for "add node ip 10.0.0.12", "select model llama", "add model" (no value lists the choices), or a model configuration key once that step is shown.

field.description: Which field: "nodeIp", "model", or a model configuration key.

value.description: The value to put in it. Empty to ask for options.

tools.x-backend: Fills one wizard field (node IP, model, config).

tools.name: panel/wizard_next
tools.description: Go to the next step of the open Start Benchmark wizard, after checking the current step. Never starts the run.
tools.x-backend: Moves the wizard on (validates; never starts the run).

tools.name: panel/prefill_jupyter_launch
tools.description: Open the Launch Jupyter page with the node IP filled in. It never launches: the user clicks Launch.

node_ip.description: Node IP to launch Jupyter on.

tools.x-backend: POST /api/v1/jupyter/launch needs node_ip.
tools.x-frontend: Navigate to Launch Jupyter and set the form's nodeIp field.

tools.name: panel/view_jupyter_progress
tools.description: Show the live launch logs of a Jupyter instance.
tools.x-backend: GET /api/v1/jupyter/instances/{task_id}/logs/stream (SSE) and /status. Follows start_jupyter.

tools.name: panel/open_notebook
tools.description: Open a READY Jupyter notebook in a new browser tab.
tools.x-backend: GET /api/v1/jupyter/instances returns jupyter_url for READY instances.
tools.x-frontend: Look up the instance in the cached list (or refetch) and window.open(jupyter_url).

tools.name: panel/open_jupyter_assistant
tools.description: Open the always-on Jupyter Lab with the Jupyter AI assistant.
tools.x-backend: GET /api/v1/jupyter/assistant returns { url, configured }.
tools.x-frontend: Fetch the URL, window.open it; say so if not configured.

tools.name: panel/confirm_delete_run
tools.description: Ask the user to confirm deleting a benchmark run's results. Opens the same confirmation dialog as the Delete button; nothing is deleted unless the user confirms.
tools.x-backend: DELETE /api/v1/benchmarks/{run_id}. A destructive action stays a human click (the backend's own rule: destructive needs approval).
tools.x-frontend: Open the DeleteRunButton's confirm modal for that run.

tools.name: panel/confirm_delete_jupyter
tools.description: Ask the user to confirm stopping and deleting a Jupyter instance. Nothing happens unless the user confirms.
tools.x-backend: DELETE /api/v1/jupyter/instances/{task_id}.
tools.x-frontend: Open the DeleteJupyterInstanceButton's confirm modal for that instance.

tools.name: panel/open_blog_post
tools.description: Open the blog post that best matches a topic.

query.description: Topic or title words, e.g. "pcie topology".

tools.x-backend: Frontend content; no backend.

tools.name: panel/set_color_scheme
tools.description: Switch between light and dark mode.
tools.x-backend: Frontend only.

tools.name: panel/set_theme
tools.description: Customise the whole app theme. Pass only what should change; "default" restores a field.

primaryColor.description: Accent colour: a Mantine palette (teal, grape...) or any CSS colour.

radius.description: Corner radius: 0, xs, sm, md, lg, xl or a length.

textScale.description: Text size multiplier (e.g. "1.1"), or "up" / "down" to step it.

tools.x-backend: Frontend only.

tools.name: panel/reset_theme
tools.description: Restore the default theme (colour, font, corners, text size).
tools.x-backend: Frontend only.

tools.name: panel/reset_styles
tools.description: Undo every style change CoreMind has made.
tools.x-backend: Frontend only.
